findings.description: The database password is interpolated into EC2 user data and written to /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. User data can be retrieved by principals or processes with access to the instance metadata service, launch-template/instance configuration, or Terraform state, exposing the database credential.

The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, assigning it a publicly reachable database endpoint. Although the shown security-group ingress is limited to the VPC CIDR, public exposure creates unnecessary external attack surface and can become reachable if network controls change.
The RDS instance explicitly sets storage_encrypted = false, leaving database storage, snapshots, and automated backups unencrypted at rest.

The database security group permits all outbound protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0. This allows a compromised database host to initiate arbitrary outbound connections rather than limiting egress to required destinations.

The policy grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* against every resource to the role attached to aws_instance.catalog_app_server. Compromise of the application server or its instance credentials would grant broad control of S3, EC2, and RDS resources, including actions that can expose or modify data and infrastructure.
